why: The must_catch list has one item: line 1 should FAIL because returning {} would make the app start on defaults, and nobody would learn which file is broken or where the mistake is. The output marks line 1 as "FAIL". Its evidence says that with this build "app.js spreads {} over DEFAULTS and prints `listening on 8080` with no message at all, so the typo is hidden completely." It ties this to the request's real need: "people can't tell which file is broken or where the mistake is." It also proposes a missing line requiring an error that names the file path and the line/column. The wrong_build section repeats the point. The trap is caught in full.
